objective: Determine without training whether a public cost distinction makes the required generic route causally identifiable to the c1l router while preserving specialist routing.

causal_basis.finding: c1l routes every table, source, and recursive-manager task correctly but sends both plain-JSON generic tasks to table_analyst. All three workers currently have equal cost and overlapping file/Python affordances, so generic is not uniquely cheapest sufficient from public evidence.

public_intervention.interpretation: Generic becomes uniquely cheaper for work it can handle. Its published limitations still exclude reconciliation and source structure, so specialists remain necessary for their niches.

decision_rule.if_screen_passes: Implement the public cost contract in the live specialist registry and run a fresh end-to-end split-scaffold population evaluation before any promotion.
decision_rule.if_screen_fails: Do not train further. Move generic-versus-specialist shortlisting into a deterministic capability-envelope scaffold or redesign the worker affordances so wrong routes fail causally.
decision_rule.promotion_requires: A later live end-to-end population evaluation with at least four complete qualifying trajectories.
